body:
Fixes #237 - Improved the application's visual appearance and added branding icons throughout.

## Changes

### 1. Enhanced UI Styling with Vibrant Colors

The application previously had a plain, monochromatic interface with small buttons. This PR transforms it into a modern, colorful application:

**Sidebar improvements:**
- Added blue background (#2E86AB) to the navigation sidebar
- Updated title styling with larger, bold white text
- Increased sidebar width from 200px to 220px for better spacing

**Button enhancements:**
- Replaced small `ttk.Button` widgets with larger, colorful `tk.Button` widgets
- Made buttons **twice as tall** (`height=2`) for easier clicking
- Applied pink/magenta background (#A23B72) with white text
- Added orange hover effect (#F18F01) for visual feedback
- Increased font size to 10pt bold for better readability
- Added hand cursor on hover for improved UX

### 2. Icon Integration Across All Windows

Added the `logo.ico` file to all tkinter windows throughout the application:

**Main window:**
- Created `set_window_icon()` method in `CordiaxApp` class
- Icon properly loads in both development (script) and production (PyInstaller) modes

**Dialog windows:**
All 8 dialog classes now display the icon:
- StudentDialog (students.py)
- AssistanceDialog (assistance.py)
- MaterialDialog (materials.py)
- MenuDialog (cafeteria.py)
- MessageDialog & ViewMessageDialog (messages.py)
- PermissionDialog & template generation dialog (permissions.py)

**PyInstaller configuration:**
- Added `datas=[('logo.ico', '.')]` to bundle icon with executable
- Set `icon='logo.ico'` to apply icon to the compiled .exe file

The icon implementation handles both environments gracefully:
- Uses `sys._MEIPASS` path when running as PyInstaller executable
- Uses relative `__file__` path when running as Python script
- Silently continues if icon fails to load (no crashes)

## Screenshot

![Cordiax UI with new colorful styling](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5fe126a-e71f-4abd-b80a-76143bc216a5)

The application now features a professional, modern interface with a blue sidebar, vibrant pink navigation buttons, and the logo icon on all windows.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

Migrated MCP tool output from structured JSON-like Markdown to LLM-optimized blockquote format, achieving **45% token reduction** while improving clarity and preventing content ambiguity.

## The Problem

The architecture doc states plainly: **"BlueSky data is too rich and verbose for LLM."** Previous output mixed user content with tool structure, creating two critical issues:

1. **Token inefficiency**: Verbose JSON-like formatting consumed unnecessary tokens
2. **Content ambiguity**: User posts containing Markdown syntax could be confused with tool structure

Consider a post containing:
```
## Features
- Fast
- Simple
```

Previous format made it unclear whether `## Features` was a tool section header or user content.

## The Solution

Adopted **blockquote prefix format** (`>`) to clearly delimit user-generated content from tool structure, following the specification in `docs/16-mcp-schemas.md`.

### Output Transformation

**Before (v0.3.2):**
```markdown
## Post 1
**URI:** [at://did:plc:test/app.bsky.feed.post/abc123](https://bsky.app/...)
**Created:** 2024-01-01T10:00:00Z

Hello world, this is a test post

**Images:**
- Sunset photo
```

**After (v0.3.3):**
```markdown
@alice.bsky.social/abc123
> Hello world, this is a test post
> ![Sunset photo](image)
2024-01-01T10:00:00Z
```

## Implementation

### Core Changes

- **Post format**: User text blockquoted line-by-line with `>` prefix
- **Profile descriptions**: Multiline descriptions now blockquoted for safety
- **Post identifiers**: Compact `@handle/rkey` format instead of full URIs
- **Images**: Included inside blockquotes as Markdown images
- **Metadata**: Timestamps and stats outside blockquotes

### Both Servers Updated

- ✅ **Rust**: Updated `PostRecord::to_markdown()` and `ProfileRecord::to_markdown()`
- ✅ **Go**: Updated `formatSearchResults()` and `formatProfileMarkdown()`

## Benefits

- 📉 **45% fewer tokens** than JSON format (measured on real data)
- 🎯 **LLM-native**: Natural language format, not schemas  
- 🔍 **Scannable**: `👍 14` beats `{"likes": {"count": 14}}`
- 🛡️ **Unambiguous**: Blockquotes clearly separate user content from structure
- 📚 **Familiar**: `>` is standard Markdown, LLMs trained on this convention

## Testing & Quality

- ✅ All 126 Rust tests passing (added blockquote format tests)
- ✅ All Go tests passing (added format validation tests)
- ✅ Zero clippy warnings
- ✅ Both release builds successful
- ✅ Documentation updated with examples

## Breaking Change ⚠️

This is a **breaking change** for MCP clients consuming tool output. Clients should expect:
- User content prefixed with `>` (blockquote)
- Compact `@handle/rkey` post identifiers
- Metadata outside blockquotes

## Version

Bumped to **v0.3.3** with updated CHANGELOGs and READMEs documenting the migration.

## Overview

This PR resolves the merge conflict in `vision-gateway/app/main.py` from PR #9 by integrating the Computer Control Agent API endpoint into the current main branch codebase.

## Problem

PR #9 introduces a Computer Control Agent that requires access to screenshots from the vision-gateway service. The PR adds functionality to `vision-gateway/app/main.py`, but was based on an older version of the code that had a `process_frame()` function. The current main branch has refactored this code and uses `hdmi_loop()` directly, causing a merge conflict.

## Solution

This PR adapts PR #9's vision-gateway changes to work with the current main branch structure:

### Changes Made

1. **Added `latest_frames` global dictionary** to store the most recent frame from each source:
   ```python
   latest_frames: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
   ```

2. **Store HDMI frames** in the `hdmi_loop()` function when frames are successfully captured:
   ```python
   latest_frames["hdmi"] = {
       "image_b64": b64_jpg(frame),
       "timestamp": time.time()
   }
   ```

3. **Added new API endpoint** `/api/latest_frame/{source}` to retrieve the latest frame:
   ```python
   @app.get("/api/latest_frame/{source}")
   def get_latest_frame(source: str):
       # Returns base64-encoded image with timestamp
   ```

## Technical Details

- **Location adapted**: Instead of a non-existent `process_frame()` function, frame storage was added directly in `hdmi_loop()` after successful frame capture (line 303)
- **Functionality preserved**: The API endpoint works identically to PR #9's design
- **No breaking changes**: All existing functionality remains unchanged
- **Type safety**: Uses proper type hints (`Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]`)

The Computer Control Agent can now retrieve screenshots from vision-gateway:

```python
response = requests.get(f"{VISION_GATEWAY_URL}/api/latest_frame/hdmi")
data = response.json()

```

Each file can be right-clicked to get a context menu that provides different actions depending on the file change (deleted/added/modified). You can also click the diff button in the files changed header to open all changes in the multi_buffer. This is incredibly useful, but I'm not sure if there needs to be a limit on how many files it could potentially open.. body:
## What It Does

Add `EndSynchronizedUpdate` to the list of executed commands for `impl Drop for StdTerminal`. 

In the general `terminal_render_loop`, terminal executes an enter to synchronized update, but the render may panic mid-update (for example, https://github.com/ccbrown/iocraft/issues/103), which usually causes `StdTerminal` to drop. But it never ends synchronized update which can cause issues. 

In my case, I was trying to run something akin to https://github.com/ccbrown/iocraft/pull/114 in alacritty + zellij, panic mid-update would freeze the terminal rendering (but it would accept input still); just alacritty worked as expected though (so I think it's zellij related, but I have no idea actually how). Ending synchronized update fixed the issue !

## Related Issues

- Originally discovered while trying to panic safely in a fullscreen app: https://github.com/ccbrown/iocraft/issues/103

body: Currently, the `SqlQueryEditor` only supports two dropdown fields, namely dataset and table. However, a plugin now needs not only to use three dropdowns, but also it doesn't need to use the dataset field. Ideally, we should make the component more versatile and extensible, allowing support for a variable number of fields (dropdowns). Even before the changes in this PR, in fact, the dataset field is already an optional field, which can be enabled or disabled using the `disableDatasets` property (of the `DB` type). This seems further prove that we need a refactoring of the component, but that is a more invasive work that could potentially introducing breaking changes that might affect several plugins, thus to be agreed on. As such, as a more pragmatic approach and to avoid blocking a user-facing feature for too long, this PR adds a `disableCatalogs` property, similarly to the `disableDatasets` one. We can then consider working on the refactoring in a separate PR, after discussing it and agreeing on the design choices to implement. Open to discussion and improvements though.
